title: Elder personas: who you'll meet and how to handle them
summary: The 7 types of elders PeakAge companions meet, what each one needs, and what never to do.
offline_note: Each persona is practised as a role-play in the offline session.

lessons.title: Why personas matter
lessons.body:
The same sentence can win one uncle and annoy another. Personas help you recognise who you're with in the first few minutes and adjust.

Two things are true for **every** persona:

1. **Everyone wants to be heard.** Ask about them first.
2. **The trust curve.** Guarded first, comfortable later. Don't rush.

> Elders are people, not boxes. A persona is a starting guess. Watch and adjust.

lessons.title: Saheb, Kissa-go and Shant Sajjan
lessons.body:
### 1. Saheb: the proud patriarch
- **Nature:** ego, stubborn, suspicious at first, attached once comfortable
- **Needs:** respect, and to feel he's still in charge
- **Win him:** listen to his stories, praise him, agree on small things, steer gently
- **Never:** argue, correct him in front of others, rush him
- **Watch:** over-attachment (“sirf wahi ladka chahiye”)

### 2. Kissa-go: the warm storyteller
- **Nature:** aware, smart, warm, loves sharing experiences
- **Needs:** an intelligent listener
- **Win him:** ask about his life and work, show real curiosity
- **Never:** look bored or check your phone
- **Watch:** the visit turning into a 2-hour chat while the work slips. Keep it on time.

### 3. Shant Sajjan: the quiet one
- **Nature:** silent at first, opens up when asked, not tech-savvy
- **Needs:** someone who starts the conversation, plus help with the app and bookings
- **Win him:** easy questions about family, past work, his city; handle tech without making him feel slow
- **Never:** stay silent too. The visit becomes transactional.

lessons.title: Bhole Babu and Akeli Amma
lessons.body:
### 4. Bhole Babu / Bholi Amma: the trusting follower
- **Nature:** uneducated or semi-educated, naive, trusts doctors blindly, can't follow details, may not speak English
- **Needs:** a translator and advocate
- **Win them:** explain in simple Hindi, write instructions down, check every bill, act like their own son or daughter
- **Never:** assume they understood
- **Watch:** misunderstood medicines, overcharging

### 5. Akeli Amma: the lonely confidante
- **Nature:** welcoming, repeats herself, vents about family, overthinks, feels guilty about money, obeys her child
- **Needs:** emotional company, listening without judgement
- **Win her:** patience, warmth. “Shanti didi ne bola hai” (the child's name) often gets cooperation.
- **Never:** say “aap yeh bata chuke ho”, take sides in family matters, accept cash
- **Watch:** her mood across visits. Report it if it gets worse.

lessons.title: Shakki/Kanjoos and Bimaar-Chidchida
lessons.body:
### 6. Shakki / Kanjoos: the suspicious, money-tight one
- **Nature:** questions every rupee, thinks “yeh log loot rahe hain”
- **Needs:** transparency
- **Win him:** show every bill before payment, photograph every receipt, payments only through the app or the child
- **Never:** get defensive. Show, don't argue.

### 7. Bimaar-Chidchida: sick, depressed and cranky
- **Nature:** dependent and resistant at the same time. The hardest case.
- **Needs:** patience and a senior companion
- **Rule:** only senior companions are assigned, with the coordinator involved
- **Watch:** red flags (see the Emergency module). Irritability can be a sign of pain or illness.

### Quick reference
| Persona | One line |
| --- | --- |
| Saheb | Respect him, never argue |
| Kissa-go | Listen, but keep on task |
| Shant Sajjan | You start the conversation |
| Bhole Babu | Translate, advocate, check every bill |
| Akeli Amma | Listen patiently, never take sides |
| Shakki/Kanjoos | App payments only, show bills |
| Bimaar-Chidchida | Senior companion with coordinator support |

questions.text: Uncle says proudly, “Main 30 saal bank manager raha hoon, mujhe mat sikhao.” Which persona is this most likely?
questions.explanation: Ego and wanting to stay in charge are signs of Saheb. Respect him, never argue.

questions.text: Aunty tells you the same story for the third time. What do you say?
options: Listen as if it's the first time
questions.explanation: Never say ‘aap bata chuke ho’. If repetition gets worse over visits, quietly tell the coordinator.

questions.text: Uncle hasn't said a word in 10 minutes of the cab ride. What should you do?
options: Start with easy questions about his family or past work
questions.explanation: Shant Sajjan opens up when asked. Don't match his silence.

questions.text: Uncle nods at everything the doctor says but can't tell you afterwards what was said. Which persona, and what do you do?
options: Bhole Babu; explain in simple Hindi and write it down
questions.explanation: Bhole Babu trusts blindly but doesn't follow details. Translate and write it down.

questions.text: A suspicious uncle asks, “Tumne zyada toh nahi diya?” What's the best response?
options: Show him the bill and receipt and check it together
questions.explanation: With Shakki/Kanjoos, show, don't argue. Transparency builds trust.

questions.text: Kissa-go uncle has been sharing stories for 40 minutes and you need to leave for the hospital. What do you do?
options: Keep listening and miss the appointment
Warmly suggest continuing the story in the cab
questions.explanation: Enjoy his stories but keep the visit on time.

questions.text: Aunty doesn't want to go for her test. She always listens to her daughter Shanti. What can help?
options: Say “Shanti didi ne bola hai ki test zaroori hai”
questions.explanation: For compliant parents like Akeli Amma, the child's voice is a lever. (It can backfire with a Saheb.)

questions.text: Who should be assigned to a sick, depressed and cranky elder (Bimaar-Chidchida)?
options: Only a senior companion, with the coordinator involved
questions.explanation: This is the hardest persona. Only seniors, with coordinator oversight.

questions.text: Saheb uncle insists on a route to the hospital that's 10 minutes longer. It's not unsafe. What do you do?
options: Go his way; it's a small thing
questions.explanation: Bend on small things. Agreeing builds trust with a Saheb.

options: They all want to be heard
questions.explanation: Everyone wants to be heard. Listening is the universal skill.

questions.text: Akeli Amma says her husband never helps and talks only to outsiders. What do you do?
options: Listen with empathy without taking sides
questions.explanation: Be her confidante, but never take sides in family matters.

questions.text: Shant Sajjan uncle struggles to use the app to see his booking. What's the right approach?
options: Do it quickly and say “bas itna sa hai”
Help patiently without making him feel slow
Tell him to ask his son
questions.explanation: Handle the tech for him without making him feel slow.
